---
title: "{{< fa brands r-project >}} Step 6: Connect your R session"
---

[Due by **{{< var due.setup >}}**]{.highlight-yellow}

Claude Code has no {{< gl "R session" >}} of its own. It can run a script or {{< gl render >}} a Quarto document, but it cannot see the data frame you have open in RStudio. The {{< gl mcptools >}} package changes that. It lets the {{< gl agent >}} run R code inside your running RStudio session and look at the objects there, which is how it inspects your data on the day. This connection is specific to R and RStudio, see the note on the [Prepare](index.qmd) page. If you work in another language or editor, the agent still works, but this step may not apply.

## {{< fa download >}} Part 1: Install the package

Open RStudio. The **Console** is the pane at the bottom left, the one with a `>` prompt. Click into it, type the line below, and press Enter. Wait until the download messages stop and the prompt is back:

```r
install.packages("mcptools")
```

## {{< fa plug >}} Part 2: Register it with Claude Code

::: {.panel-tabset}

### macOS

Open the {{< gl terminal display="Terminal" >}} app (Spotlight, then type Terminal). Any folder is fine, this setting is not tied to a folder. Copy the line below, paste it after the prompt, and press Enter. It answers with a line saying the server was added:

```bash
claude mcp add -s user r-mcptools -- Rscript -e "mcptools::mcp_server()"
```

### Windows

Open {{< gl PowerShell >}} (Start menu, then type PowerShell). On Windows the `Rscript` program is usually not findable from the {{< gl terminal >}}, so you give the full path. Get it from the RStudio {{< gl Console >}}, the pane at the bottom left:

```r
normalizePath(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript.exe"))
```

It prints something like `C:\Program Files\R\R-4.5.1\bin\Rscript.exe`. Use your path, in quotes, in PowerShell:

```powershell
claude mcp add -s user r-mcptools -- "C:\Program Files\R\R-4.5.1\bin\Rscript.exe" -e "mcptools::mcp_server()"
```

:::

Check, in the same terminal:

```bash
claude mcp list
```

The line for `r-mcptools` should end in **Connected**.

## {{< fa gear >}} Part 3: Let R announce its sessions

The server needs to know which {{< gl "R session" >}} to talk to. One line in your {{< gl "R profile" >}} registers every RStudio session you start.

Back in RStudio, click into the {{< gl Console >}} and run:

```r
file.edit("~/.Rprofile")
```

A file called `.Rprofile` opens in the editor pane at the top left. It is empty unless you have set up R this way before. Paste this line into it, then save with **Cmd+S** on macOS or **Ctrl+S** on Windows:

```r
if (interactive()) mcptools::mcp_session()
```

Restart R from the menu bar: **Session, Restart R**. The Console clears and shows a fresh prompt. Then, in the Console, create something for the {{< gl agent >}} to look at:

```r
x <- head(mtcars)
```

## {{< fa vial >}} Part 4: Try it

Check the **Environment** pane at the top right of RStudio: `x` is listed there as 6 obs. of 11 variables. Now open a {{< gl terminal >}} at your setup {{< gl repository >}} (as in step 4), start `claude`, and ask:

> What objects are in my R session?

If Claude Code asks before using the r-mcptools tool, read the prompt and allow it; in {{< gl "auto mode" >}} it runs without asking. The answer names `x` and describes it as a data frame with 6 rows and 11 columns. On the day you do the same with the workshop data loaded.

::: {.callout-important}
## What this connection means

With this in place the {{< gl agent >}} can run any R code in your live session, including code that removes objects or writes files. In {{< gl "manual mode" >}} the {{< gl permission >}} prompt is what stands between it and that; in {{< gl "auto mode" >}} a built-in check takes that role, and it does not know your data. Read what the agent proposes, or what it did, rather than approving by reflex. That habit is the point of the workshop, and this is where you start it.
:::
